learning_objective: The learner will classify each of 10 statements about generating a textbook as describing a cost, a price, or a quality, with at least 9 of 10 correct.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** cost-price-quality-sorter
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Template:** https://github.com/dmccreary/token-efficiency/tree/main/docs/sims/cost-quality-pareto-frontier
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** classify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will classify each of 10 statements about generating a textbook as describing a cost, a price, or a quality, with at least 9 of 10 correct. **Prerequisites:** cost, price, quality (defined in the section above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each of the 10 statements the learner commits one label, "Cost", "Price", or "Quality", before the sim reveals the answer. A label is correct when it equals the Correct label column. Mastery is 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt. Reading a statement is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A number in dollars must be a price. (2) A service's charge tells you what delivering the service costs it. (3) A generated text that builds without errors is good. **Instructional Rationale:** Classifying a statement shows the learner has constructed the distinction, and mixed items in dollars and in non-money terms prevent a shortcut based on the unit of the number. Committing before the reveal separates understanding from recognition. **Content:** | # | Statement shown to the learner | Correct label | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | The unit used about 832 kWh of electricity in a year. | Cost | It is what the owner spends to operate the machine. | | 2 | A provider charges a fixed fee for each million tokens generated. | Price | It is what a provider asks of a customer for a service. | | 3 | The generated learning graph has 200 concepts and no dependency cycles. | Quality | It describes how good the output is. | | 4 | Setting up the machine took 40 hours of labor at $90 an hour. | Cost | It is effort the owner spends to put the machine into use. | | 5 | A subscription lets one user generate chapters for a flat monthly amount. | Price | It is the provider's charge for access to a service. | | 6 | A reviewer found every worked example in the chapter correct. | Quality | It describes how good the output is. | | 7 | The hardware loses its value evenly over three years. | Cost | Depreciation is what owning the asset uses up. | | 8 | A service adds a 20% margin to what it costs the service to generate a book. | Price | The margin is part of what the provider charges. | | 9 | Chapter prose stays at the stated reading level across 10,000 words. | Quality | It describes how good the output is. | | 10 | An uninterruptible power supply and cabling add $250 to the purchase. | Cost | It is spent by the owner to run the machine. | **Provenance:** The statements are synthetic, written for this exercise, and the sim labels them "synthetic example". Numeric values match the cost analysis page and the sections of this chapter. **Rules:** Statements are shown in the fixed order 1 to 10. Each statement allows exactly one label, and the label is final. A statement is correct when its label equals the Correct label column. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner reads statement 1. 2. The learner chooses "Cost", "Price", or "Quality" and confirms. 3. The sim shows the correct label and the Why text, and marks the statement correct or incorrect. 4. The learner repeats for statements 2 to 10. After statement 10 the sim shows the score and, for each miss, the misconception behind it. **Feedback:** Ten statements, fixed order, one confirmed label each, no second attempt. Correct: "Correct" followed by the Why text. Incorrect: "Not quite" followed by the correct label and the Why text. The final score reads "n of 10 correct". **Starting State:** Statement 1 is shown with no label chosen, and the question on screen is "Is this a cost, a price, or a quality?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter states that cost is what you pay to own and operate, price is what a provider charges, and quality is how good the output is, and that these are three different things.
